style_when: the story is regulatory or contractual — a filing, a mandate, a rate notice, a certificate, a purchase order that changed the economics
prompt: Overhead flat-lay photograph, top-down 90-degree view, 50mm flat field optic with a razor-sharp focal plane. Symmetrical top-down composition of a layered stack of heavy institutional documents on a matte grey steel desk. A thick, embossed customs ledger pins down overlapping translucent carrier scans and temperature logs, one paper slightly out of alignment to look handled. Even diffused daylight from above, muted paper tones, illegible cropped text, tactile paper stock with visible fiber.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, typography, people, hands, faces
rationale: The story is entirely about regulatory clocks, document retention rules, and joined records. A flat-lay of layered documents perfectly visualizes the overlapping legal burdens.
cue: longest legal clock among those inputs
subject: an overlapping stack of heavy institutional documents and carrier scans
core_thesis: The retention of a control tower's joined exception log is dictated by the longest legal clock among its inputs, typically the five-year customs rule.
core_conflict: Short-term operational data storage versus long-term regulatory compliance clocks.
